finding.problem: The chosen environment is never used downstream. Delivery's `preview` and `deploy` kernel calls pass only domain, commit and approver (deploy) and carry no environment. Delivery has no action that sets Environment.current_commit either. While `local` was the only value this made no difference. Now a `staging` request gets the same preview and deploy as `local`, so delivering to staging may deploy to the wrong place or have no effect on a shared environment. The request's stated purpose, a separate shared environment before real users, is not met.
finding.where: SKILL.md, Delivery Actions `preview` and `deploy` (kernel call arguments); Authoring `deliver` (environment enum) and the Handoff parameters

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: The seeded answer is 'none', and the request only asks to allow staging in the enum; whether downstream calls carry the environment is outside this change's scope and not a demonstrated breakage.

finding.problem: The Delivery world has only the Environment `ENV-local`, and every DeliveryRequest fixture (R1–R4) uses `local`. There is no `staging` Environment fixture and no example or scenario that delivers to staging. The new enum value is untested and has nothing in the world for a staging request to point at.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Missing staging fixtures or examples is not a defect in allowing the enum value; the seeded answer is none and this is only a test-coverage gap.

finding.problem: Delivery still describes a single environment. The purpose says versions reach 'the environment', and the glossary says a deploy puts a commit 'into an environment'. The `deploy floor` and the `deploy` rule apply the same fixed floor to every environment. Nothing says staging differs from local or whether staging comes before the people who use the domain. The Handoff also still passes `params.environment` unvalidated into a free-form string field, so Delivery would accept any value.

findings.label: false-alarm
findings.why: Docs still describing a single environment and the unvalidated string field are pre-existing or cosmetic, not a real conflict caused by adding the enum value.

edit.why: The edit adds staging to the deliver action's environment enum alongside local, which is exactly what the request asked for.
